params.name: command
params.description: The command line, typed as a paste and submitted with Enter. One line, no control characters: join several commands with ; or &&.

params.name: timeout
params.description: Milliseconds to wait for the command to finish before failing with the timeout code. The command keeps running after a timeout.

params.name: lines
params.description: Keep only the last N lines of the output.

returns.name: exit_code
returns.description: The status the shell reported. Omitted when the shell sent none, which a bash integration does on ctrl+c.

returns.name: output
returns.description: What the command printed, as plain text, read from the pane between the shell's marks. At most the last 256 KiB.

returns.name: truncated
returns.description: True when the output was cut, or its start had already left the scrollback.

returns.name: cmdline
returns.description: The command line as the shell showed it, cut to 512 bytes with likely secrets masked.

returns.name: duration_ms
returns.description: How long the command ran, from the shell's marks.

returns.name: command_seq
returns.description: How many commands the pane has finished, this one included.

returns.name: window
returns.description: Id of the pane the command ran in.

returns.name: session
returns.description: The session the pane is in.

run-command.description: Run one tape command, or any keybinding action by the name config.toml binds it to. Prefer a verb where one exists: a verb reports what changed, this reports only that the command ran.

params.name: session
params.description: Session name. Omit from a pane for the pane's own session, and from outside every pane for the most recently active one.

params.name: command
params.description: Tape command name, e.g. "ToggleZoom" or "SnapLeft", or a keybinding action name, e.g. "toggle_spotlight" (tuios keybinds list prints them). An action runs on an attached client. Only a user action (user:NAME) takes args, each key=value.

params.name: args
params.description: Arguments for the command.

returns.name: command
returns.description: The command that ran.

returns.name: routed
returns.description: True when an attached client ran it, false when the daemon did.

screenshot.description: Render a window to an image file.

params.name: session
params.description: Session name. Omit from a pane for the pane's own session, and from outside every pane for the most recently active one.

params.name: window
params.description: Window id or name. Omit to target the focused window.

params.name: format
params.description: Output format.

params.name: frame
params.description: Dressing around the capture.

params.name: theme
params.description: Render in this theme instead of the session's. Truecolor cells are unchanged by it.

params.name: scrollback
params.description: Put the pane's history above the screen in the picture.

params.name: lines
params.description: Bound the history rows to the last N. Needs scrollback.

params.name: cursor
params.description: Draw the cursor cell.

params.name: out
params.description: Write here instead of generating a name under screenshot.directory. A linked machine cannot set it.

returns.name: path
returns.description: The file that was written.

returns.name: host
returns.description: The machine the path is on: daemon or client.

returns.name: format
returns.description: The format that was rendered.

returns.name: cols
returns.description: Grid width in cells.

returns.name: rows
returns.description: Grid height in cells, history included.

returns.name: bytes
returns.description: Size of the written file.

returns.name: warnings
returns.description: Anything the render had to guess or fall back on. Empty when there is nothing to say.

select-workspace.description: Show a workspace. To rename or reorder workspaces, use set-workspace-name and set-workspace-order.

params.name: session
params.description: Session name. Omit from a pane for the pane's own session, and from outside every pane for the most recently active one.

params.name: workspace
params.description: Workspace number to show.

params.name: return_to
params.description: Workspace to show when this workspace loses its last pane, before any other. tuios xpanes sets it to the workspace that ran it.

returns.name: current_workspace
returns.description: Workspace now showing.

returns.name: focused_window_id
returns.description: Window focused on it, empty when it holds none.

returns.name: window_count
returns.description: How many windows it holds.

send-agent-message.description: Leave a message in a session's agent ring, addressed to one window's inbox or, with no recipient, to the session as a notice. With select and confirm it goes to every agent pane a selector matches, each in its own session's ring. It queues rather than typing, so it is safe to send to an agent that is mid-turn. A pane with the mail grant sends to any session on this daemon, always as itself, and attaches to another session's mail only files in its own folder or its session's stash.

params.name: session
params.description: Session name. Omit from a pane for the pane's own session, and from outside every pane for the most recently active one.

params.name: to
params.description: Recipient window id or name, or human for the person at the attached client. Omit to post a notice everyone in the session can read.

params.name: from
params.description: The sending window, normally $TUIOS_PANE_ID. It is a claim the daemon cannot verify, and it is what the rate cap and the loop guards are keyed on. From another machine it is kept as a label and not resolved. human from a process inside a pane of this daemon is refused with forbidden.

params.name: from_host
params.description: The name of the machine the sender is on, normally $TUIOS_HOST. Kept only for a send that arrived over a link, as the sender's own claim.

params.name: subject
params.description: Optional one-line summary, at most 120 characters.

params.name: text
params.description: The message body, at most 8 KiB. Required without parts. With parts it is ignored.

params.name: parts
params.description: The message in ordered parts, as queue-prompt takes them: text, paste and image. When the whole message fits 8 KiB and holds no image, the blocks are put in their place. Otherwise each paste and image is written to the paste folder on this machine, kept for 24 hours, attached to the message, and named in the body: [Pasted text #1: PATH, 42 lines], [Image #1: PATH]. The attachments, given and written, are at most 8. From a linked machine, writing a file needs files in its policy.

params.name: reply_to
params.description: The id of the message this one answers. The reply joins that message's thread, and a reply to a reply joins the same one. A reply is the only acknowledgement between agents that means anything.

params.name: attachments
params.description: Absolute paths to existing files on the daemon's host. The ring stores the reference, never the bytes, so the producer keeps the file.

params.name: human_nonce
params.description: The nonce from an attach reply, which the tuios client sends with a reply from its mail overlay. A message from human is stored as verified_human only when this matches a client attached to the session now, over the same kind of connection, the sender is outside every pane, and, where the kernel gives both pids, the sender is the process that attached. Without it, from human is stored as claimed_human.

params.name: host
params.description: A machine in the [hosts] table: deliver to session there over this machine's link, and keep the message here while the link is down or the far machine does not answer, to deliver in order. The answer is then the far machine's, with host, or queued with queue_id. session is required. from human arrives there as claimed_human. Not taken over a link, or with select.

params.name: select
params.description: A selector: space-separated key:value terms, all of which must match, each with comma-separated alternatives. Keys: harness (id or program name), state, needs:you, session (glob), group (fan-out group, glob), host (local or a host name, glob), name (window name, glob), cwd (the directory or under it; ~ is home), task (a task card the pane holds, by id, glob), stage (the stage of a card the pane holds), parent and root (the parent agent pane, or the first of its chain, by window id or a start of it). Sends one directed message to every pane the selector matches, at most 32. It reaches agent panes on this machine, in every session, and takes no session and no window. Without confirm nothing is sent: the call fails with confirm_required, whose hint lists the panes in available and carries the token in confirm.

params.name: confirm
params.description: The token for the set of panes the selector matches, from a confirm_required hint or from list-agents with the same selector. The write goes ahead only when the selector still matches exactly that set; otherwise it fails with confirm_required again and the new set.

returns.name: results
returns.description: With select: one row per pane, in session order: session, window, name, ok, and message_id and thread_id when it was sent or error (code, message, hint) when it was not. Each pane goes through the checks a single send makes, the rate cap included.

returns.name: sent
returns.description: With select: how many panes the message reached.

returns.name: failed
returns.description: With select: how many panes refused it.

returns.name: message_id
returns.description: The id of the stored message.

returns.name: queued
returns.description: With host: true when the message waits here: the link was down, the far machine did not answer, or earlier mail for it still waits.

returns.name: queue_id
returns.description: With queued: the message's place in this machine's outbox.

returns.name: waiting
returns.description: With queued: how many messages now wait for that machine.

returns.name: kind
returns.description: message for a directed message, notice for a session-wide one.

returns.name: to
returns.description: The resolved recipient window id, empty for a notice.

returns.name: to_name
returns.description: The recipient's name at the time of sending.

returns.name: from
returns.description: The resolved sender window id.

returns.name: sent_at
returns.description: Unix-nano time the message was stored.

returns.name: reply_to
returns.description: The message this one answers, zero when it answers nothing.

returns.name: thread_id
returns.description: The thread this message belongs to, which is the id of the message the thread started from. A message that starts a thread carries its own id. Pass it to the read and wait filters.

returns.name: reply_to_missing
returns.description: The message being answered had already been dropped from the ring, so the thread is rooted on the id the reply named rather than on the parent's own thread. The reply still stands.

returns.name: origin
returns.description: link when the send arrived from another machine over the daemon's link, empty when it came from this machine. The daemon decides it from the connection, never from the request.

returns.name: origin_host
returns.description: The machine name the sender claimed, for a send from another machine.

returns.name: verified_human
returns.description: True for a message from human that carried the nonce of a client attached to the session now.

returns.name: claimed_human
returns.description: True for a message from human that carried no such nonce. It is a claim anything with the socket can make.

returns.name: held
returns.description: True when this machine's link policy (hold_mail) put a message from another machine in the person's Inbox instead of the recipient's. The person passes it on with release-agent-message.

returns.name: held_for
returns.description: With held, the window the message was addressed to, empty for a notice.

send-keys.description: Send keys to a window's program: Up, PageDown, ctrl+c. With a window they go to that window's terminal; without one, to an attached client (the window manager) or else the focused window. From a pane, window is required.

params.name: session
params.description: Session name. Omit from a pane for the pane's own session, and from outside every pane for the most recently active one.

params.name: window
params.description: Window id or name. Omit to target the focused window.

params.name: keys
params.description: Keys split on spaces and commas, e.g. "Down Down PageDown" or "ctrl+c". A key is a name (Enter Tab BTab Space Comma Escape Backspace Up Down Right Left Home End PageUp PageDown Insert Delete F1-F12, case-insensitive, also as arrow-up, KEY_UP, <Up>, PgDn), one character, a name or character after ctrl+, alt+ or shift+ (or tmux C-, M-, S-), an escape sequence written \e[A, or PREFIX for the leader key. list-keys returns the full list.

params.name: literal
params.description: Send the keys to the PTY without parsing them as key names.

params.name: raw
params.description: Treat every character as its own key instead of splitting on spaces and commas.

params.name: repeat
params.description: Send the whole sequence this many times, 1 to 1000.

params.name: allow_blocked
params.description: From a pane, type into a pane on needs_input instead of refusing with agent_blocked. What is typed then answers its prompt, which also needs the respond grant. The person, outside every pane, is not held.

returns.name: sent_to
returns.description: window when the keys were written to a window's terminal, client when an attached client took them as the person's keys.

returns.name: window_id
returns.description: The window the keys were written to, when sent_to is window.

returns.name: window
returns.description: That window's name, or its title when it has no name.

returns.name: keys
returns.description: How many keys were sent, counting repeats.

send-text.description: Send literal text to a window's PTY. From a pane, window is required.

params.name: session
params.description: Session name. Omit from a pane for the pane's own session, and from outside every pane for the most recently active one.

params.name: window
params.description: Window id or name. Omit to target the focused window.

params.name: text
params.description: Text written verbatim to the PTY.

params.name: paste
params.description: Send the text as a paste. Control characters other than tab, line feed and carriage return are removed. The text is wrapped in the bracketed paste delimiters when the program in the pane turned bracketed paste on.

params.name: submit
params.description: Paste the text and submit it with the Enter key of the harness in the pane, after a short wait for the paste to be taken in, as ask-agent does.

params.name: allow_blocked
params.description: From a pane, type into a pane on needs_input instead of refusing with agent_blocked. What is typed then answers its prompt, which also needs the respond grant. The person, outside every pane, is not held.

params.name: session
params.description: Session name. Omit from a pane for the pane's own session, and from outside every pane for the most recently active one.

set-agent-meta.description: Record display metadata about the agent in a window's pane (model, context used, cost, a short summary). The rail draws it under the agent's row. It is display only: it never changes the agent state, a wait, an alert or a message. Keys keep the position they first arrived in. The metadata clears when the agent leaves the pane. A call that sets keys to the values they hold changes nothing and pushes nothing to clients; a TTL is renewed only once less than half of it remains. The keys now and prompt are written by tuios from hook activity and are refused here.

params.name: session
params.description: Session name. Omit from a pane for the pane's own session, and from outside every pane for the most recently active one.

params.name: window
params.description: Window id or name. Omit to target the focused window.

params.name: tokens
params.description: Key to value. A string sets the key, null removes it. At most 16 keys per call and 32 per pane. A key is 1 to 24 lower-case letters, digits, '_' or '-', starting with a letter, and not now, prompt or subagents. A value has control characters replaced and is cut to 80 characters. Required unless clear is true.

params.name: source
params.description: Who is writing, recorded on each key so clear can remove only this writer's keys.

params.name: ttl_ms
params.description: Milliseconds the keys set by this call live before the daemon drops them. 0 keeps them until they are removed or the agent leaves. At most one day.

params.name: clear
params.description: Remove every key this source wrote, or every key when source is empty, before applying tokens. The keys tuios writes, now, prompt and subagents, stay.

returns.name: window_id
returns.description: The window the metadata was recorded on.

returns.name: meta
returns.description: The keys the pane holds after the call, key to value.

returns.name: truncated
returns.description: The keys whose values were cut to the length limit.

set-agent-quiet.description: Mark a window quiet, or clear the mark. A quiet window opens no finished, question or errored item in the Inbox, and its open items of those kinds close. A pane that calls this leaves an open question open. Its agent state and agent-state events do not change, and an approval or a login still reaches the person. The window must run an agent. Needs the admin grant.

params.name: session
params.description: Session name. Omit from a pane for the pane's own session, and from outside every pane for the most recently active one.

params.name: window
params.description: Window id or name. Omit to target the focused window.

params.name: quiet
params.description: True marks the window quiet, and false clears the mark. Clearing it opens no old item, except a question the pane waits on now.

returns.name: session
returns.description: The session that holds the window.

returns.name: window_id
returns.description: The window that was marked.

returns.name: quiet
returns.description: Whether the window is now quiet.

returns.name: closed
returns.description: How many open Inbox items this call closed.

set-agent-session.description: Store the conversation id a harness reports for a window's pane, without changing the pane's agent state, its source or its harness attribution. It is what a hook sends for a harness whose hooks are trusted to name the conversation but not to report its state. The id is stored and persisted as the window's agent_session_id, the same field set-agent-state's agent_session_id writes.

params.name: session
params.description: Session name. Omit from a pane for the pane's own session, and from outside every pane for the most recently active one.

params.name: window
params.description: Window id or name. Omit to target the focused window.

params.name: harness
params.description: Id of the harness the conversation belongs to. A window attributed to a different harness refuses the report with reason foreign_harness.

params.name: agent_session_id
params.description: The harness's own id for the conversation, at most 256 bytes.

params.name: transcript_path
params.description: The exact transcript file, held to set-agent-state's same-machine, own-pane, regular-file and manifest-folder rules. A transcript update never replaces a different conversation, even at rest.

params.name: transcript_leaf
params.description: Pi's selected entry, as set-agent-state describes it. An empty string selects an empty branch. Updating selection changes no agent state and raises a transcript event even without a file append.

params.name: harness_pid
params.description: The pid of the harness process that ran the hook. While the window is working or needs_input, a different id from a different process than the one that reported the stored id is a nested run and is refused with reason foreign_session. A harness whose environment names this pane in TUIOS_PANE_ID but that runs outside it, neither the pane's process nor on its terminal, with a harness daemon among its ancestors, even one the pane started (Claude Code's daemon or the pty host of its background sessions), is refused with reason foreign_pane: a background session that inherited the variable. A harness under anything else that left the pane, such as a tmux server or a rootless container's conmon, is taken for the pane. Kept in daemon memory only.

returns.name: agent_session_id
returns.description: The id the window holds after the call.

returns.name: transcript_refused
returns.description: Why the transcript update was refused. Absent when accepted or not provided.

returns.name: applied
returns.description: Whether the report was taken. A report naming the id the window already holds is taken and changes nothing.

returns.name: reason
returns.description: Why the report was not taken. Absent when it was.

set-agent-state.description: Set the agent state a window's pane reports (working, needs_input, idle, done, errored, or none to clear). A pane reports its own state by calling this against the daemon socket.

params.name: session
params.description: Session name. Omit from a pane for the pane's own session, and from outside every pane for the most recently active one.

params.name: window
params.description: Window id or name. Omit to target the focused window.

params.name: state
params.description: The agent state to record.

params.name: message
params.description: Optional short note reported with the state, e.g. what the agent is waiting for.

params.name: source
params.description: Where the state came from. A source ranked below the one that last set the window is refused. The result then reports applied false and the state that stands.

params.name: harness
params.description: Optional id of the harness the state is about, reported back by get-agent-state.

params.name: kind
params.description: What a needs_input state waits for: approval for a tool call waiting to be allowed, question for anything else. Only valid with needs_input, except usage_limit, the older way to say limit_reached: with errored or limit_reached, the report lands as limit_reached, which stops task dispatch. Omitted, it is guessed from message. Reported back by get-agent-state and list-agents as blocked_by.

params.name: agent_session_id
params.description: The harness's own id for the conversation, as a hook reports it. It is stored on the window for a later resume. It also turns on the nested-session guard: while the pane's harness is working or needs_input by its own report, a report for a different conversation or from a different harness is refused with reason foreign_session or foreign_harness.

params.name: transcript_path
params.description: The transcript file the harness is writing, as a hook reports it. For a harness whose manifest has a transcript reader, the window is joined to this exact file instead of a searched one. It must be a regular file under the harness's transcript folder, and a process in a pane may name one only for its own pane. Kept in daemon memory only.

params.name: transcript_leaf
params.description: Pi's selected tree entry id, at most 128 letters, digits, '-' or '_'. A present empty string selects the empty branch; omission preserves the previous selection or uses the last complete entry for an old hook. Requires harness pi and transcript_path. Kept in daemon memory only.

params.name: if_state
params.description: Comma-separated states. The report applies only when the window is in one of them now, and is otherwise refused with reason if_state.

params.name: subagent_id
params.description: With needs_input: the id of the subagent whose prompt the pane shows, as the harness's hook names it. Omitted, the prompt is the pane's own agent's. Kept in daemon memory only.

params.name: if_subagent_id
params.description: The report applies only while the window is on a needs_input that named this subagent_id, and is otherwise refused with reason if_state. A subagent's hook clears the prompt it raised with it, and leaves one the main agent or another subagent raised.

params.name: notification
params.description: The report comes from an event the harness sends once and never takes back, such as Claude Code's Notification and PermissionRequest hooks. Its state holds until the pane writes again, and from then on a look at the pane's title or screen may replace it, as for a desktop notification the pane sends. A needs_input marked so ends on a look only while the screen reads idle, an empty prompt box, and only once that reading has held as long as a working pane's idle must; neither the title's idle nor any working look ends it, and a hook's report ends it at once.

params.name: harness_pid
params.description: The pid of the harness process that ran the hook. With agent_session_id, a different session from the same harness process is a new conversation in that process (/clear or /resume, even after an interrupted turn that never reported Stop), so it takes the pane over instead of being refused as foreign_session. A harness whose environment names this pane in TUIOS_PANE_ID but that runs outside it, neither the pane's process nor on its terminal, with a harness daemon among its ancestors, even one the pane started (Claude Code's daemon or the pty host of its background sessions), is refused with reason foreign_pane: a background session that inherited the variable. A harness under anything else that left the pane, such as a tmux server or a rootless container's conmon, is taken for the pane. A harness_pid that is not the caller or one of its ancestors is not believed, and the caller is checked in its place. Kept in daemon memory only.

params.name: session_start
params.description: Marks the report of a conversation starting or resuming, as a SessionStart hook sends it. For a harness whose manifest sets shared_server (Codex), a report for a conversation other than the pane's own takes the pane over only with this set, and is otherwise refused with reason foreign_session.

params.name: agent_cwd
params.description: The folder the harness reported for its session (a hook payload's cwd). The first one for a session is kept as the agent's start folder, when it is the folder the pane's process runs in. The risk rules use it as the root of a pane that started in the home folder or above. Later reports never move it.

params.name: activity
params.description: One hook event of the pane's own agent, for its activity ring: event (prompt, tool, tool_done, tool_failed or turn_end), tool, target, text, files, ok and model. It is recorded whenever the report passes the identity guard, whether or not the state applies, and read back with agent-activity. It also sets the reserved metadata keys now (a tool call starting) and prompt (a prompt), and model when the harness named one. Display only. A hook sends it only to a daemon whose list-verbs lists it.

returns.name: state
returns.description: The state the window shows after the call, which is the reported one only when applied is true.

returns.name: applied
returns.description: Whether this report set the state.

returns.name: reason
returns.description: Why the report was not applied. Absent when it was.

returns.name: activity_recorded
returns.description: With activity: whether it went into the pane's activity ring. False for a report the identity guard refused. Absent without activity.

returns.name: transcript_refused
returns.description: Why the window was not joined to transcript_path. Absent when it was, or when no path was given.

returns.name: session
returns.description: The session of the window the report went to, when the daemon placed it on another window. Absent otherwise.

returns.name: window
returns.description: The window the report went to, when the window named is gone and the report is a shared_server harness's (Codex) from outside every pane. The daemon places it on the one live pane that runs its conversation: the pane that holds agent_session_id, the pane joined to transcript_path, or the pane whose agent started near the start of that transcript, in its folder. Absent otherwise.

params.name: mode

returns.name: mode

returns.name: held
returns.description: True while the daemon holds the machine awake.

returns.name: working

returns.name: method
returns.description: How the hold is made.

returns.name: error

returns.name: saved

returns.name: save_error

set-layout.description: Turn tiling on or off, tidy the splits, and shape the master-stack layout. Needs an attached client.

params.name: session
params.description: Session name. Omit from a pane for the pane's own session, and from outside every pane for the most recently active one.

params.name: tiling
params.description: Tile the panes automatically, or let them float.

params.name: equalize
params.description: Reset every split ratio so the panes share the space evenly.

params.name: rotate
params.description: Flip the axis of the split holding the focused pane.

params.name: master_position
params.description: Side the master panes take on the current workspace: left, right, top, bottom or center.

params.name: master_count
params.description: How many panes are master panes on the current workspace, 1 to 9.

returns.name: tiling_mode
returns.description: "tiling" or "floating".

returns.name: layout_mode

set-note.description: Set the return note of a session, or of one pane with window: one short line that says what it is for or what comes next. Every client shows it, the dock shows it when a person comes back to the session, and it survives a reattach and a daemon restart.

params.name: window
params.description: Window id or name for a pane's note. Omit for the session's note.

params.name: note

set-option.description: Set a configuration option. An attached client applies it live. The path and value are checked against the option registry, so a bad call fails instead of reporting success.

params.name: session
params.description: Session name. Omit from a pane for the pane's own session, and from outside every pane for the most recently active one.

params.name: key
params.description: Option path, e.g. "appearance.sidebar.enabled". Call list-options for the full set.

params.name: value
params.description: New value, as a string. Booleans take true/false/on/off/1/0/yes/no.

params.name: no_save
params.description: Apply the value without saving it. Later saves of other settings leave the key in the config files alone. The value stays until the client exits or the option is set again without no_save.

returns.name: key

returns.name: deprecated
returns.description: Why this path is deprecated and what replaced it. Present only for a deprecated path.

set-pane-grants.description: Give a pane grants, or with reset the default of [agents.permissions]. Grants are read (its own session and fan group), write (type into its own session), fan (write in its fan group and start agents), respond (answer prompts without the person's nonce) and admin (everything else, as before grants existed). From outside every pane anything may be given. A pane may change only its own grants unless it holds admin, and may never give more than it holds, so a pane cannot widen itself. Refused over a link.

params.name: session
params.description: Session of the pane. Omit from a pane for the pane's own session, and from outside every pane for the most recently active one.

params.name: window
params.description: The pane, by window id or name. Omit from a pane to mean the caller's own.

params.name: grants
params.description: The grants to give, or none for no grants at all.

params.name: reset
params.description: Give the pane the default of [agents.permissions] instead of grants of its own.

returns.name: session
returns.description: The pane's session.

returns.name: window
returns.description: The pane's window id.

returns.name: grants
returns.description: What the pane holds now.

returns.name: explicit
returns.description: False after reset: the pane holds the default and follows it when the config changes.

returns.name: previous
returns.description: What the pane held before.

returns.name: previous_explicit
returns.description: Whether what it held before was its own.

set-session-accent.description: Set a session's accent colour. Every attached client shares it, and it survives a reattach.

params.name: session
params.description: Session name. Omit from a pane for the pane's own session, and from outside every pane for the most recently active one.

params.name: accent
params.description: An ANSI colour name ("cyan", "bright blue") or a #rrggbb value, recorded verbatim. Omit or pass an empty string to clear it and let the client pick the session's colour.

set-session-name.description: Set a session's display label. The session keeps its name for addressing, persistence and TUIOS_SESSION. To change the name, use rename-session.

params.name: session
params.description: Session name. Omit from a pane for the pane's own session, and from outside every pane for the most recently active one.

params.name: name
params.description: Display label for the session. Omit or pass an empty string to clear it and fall back to the session name.

set-session-order.description: Put the sessions in an order. Every client lists them in it: the rail, go-to, tuios ls. It survives a daemon restart. A session the list leaves out, and one made later, goes after the named ones in creation order.

params.name: order
params.description: Session names in their new order. Every name must be a live session, or nothing changes. Repeats are dropped.

params.name: skip_missing
params.description: Leave out a name that is no live session, rather than refusing the order. The result lists them as missing.

returns.name: type
returns.description: Always session_order_set.

returns.name: order
returns.description: Every session's name, in the order the daemon lists them now.

returns.name: missing
returns.description: With skip_missing, the names that were no live session. Omitted when there were none.

set-session-space.description: File a session under a space, a named group of related sessions that tuios ls and the sidebar list together, or mark it global. A space exists while at least one session is in it. It survives a daemon restart with the session. A global session is in no space, and filing one is refused unless global is false.

params.name: session
params.description: Session name. Omit from a pane for the pane's own session, and from outside every pane for the most recently active one.

params.name: space
params.description: The space's name. Surrounding whitespace is trimmed, and the rest follows the session name rules (no slash, backslash or control character) and is at most 64 bytes. Omit or pass an empty string to take the session out of any space.

params.name: global
params.description: True marks the session global: it holds panes from more than one machine, is listed in its own group, and a new window in it asks which machine to run on. It takes the session out of its space, and is refused with a space. False takes the mark off before the space is set. Omit to leave the mark as it is.

returns.name: type
returns.description: Always session_space_set.

returns.name: session
returns.description: The session's name.

returns.name: space
returns.description: The space the session is in now, empty for none.

returns.name: global
returns.description: Whether the session is global now.

set-window.description: Change a window's name or minimized state. Pass only the fields to change.

params.name: session
params.description: Session name. Omit from a pane for the pane's own session, and from outside every pane for the most recently active one.

params.name: window
params.description: Window to change. Omit for the focused one.

params.name: name
params.description: New name. Pass an empty string to clear it and fall back to the shell's title.

params.name: minimized

returns.name: display_name
returns.description: The name shown now. After a clear this is the shell's title.

returns.name: minimized

set-workspace-name.description: Name a workspace. The workspace keeps its number for addressing. An unnamed workspace shows the name its active pane gave with OSC 1, else its number.

params.name: session
params.description: Session name. Omit from a pane for the pane's own session, and from outside every pane for the most recently active one.

params.name: workspace
params.description: Workspace number to name.

params.name: name
params.description: Label for the workspace. Omit or pass an empty string to clear it and fall back to the number.

set-workspace-order.description: Put the workspaces in an order, renumbering them: a workspace's number is its position. Each workspace takes its panes, name, focus and layout to its new number.

params.name: session
params.description: Session name. Omit from a pane for the pane's own session, and from outside every pane for the most recently active one.

params.name: order
params.description: Workspace numbers in their new order. The workspaces named take the numbers they hold between them, smallest first, in this order: [3,1,2] makes 3 workspace 1, 1 workspace 2 and 2 workspace 3. A workspace the list omits keeps its number. Numbers outside the session's range and repeats are dropped.

split-window.description: Split a pane and put a new one beside it. Works with no client attached, and turns tiling on when it is off. The new pane opens on the workspace of the pane it cuts, and starts in the caller's directory when cwd is left out.

params.name: session
params.description: Session name. Omit from a pane for the pane's own session, and from outside every pane for the most recently active one.

params.name: window
params.description: Window to split. Omit to split the caller's own pane, or outside a pane the focused one.

params.name: direction
params.description: Axis to cut on. The new pane goes right or below. Pass this or side.

params.name: side
params.description: Side of the pane the new pane takes. Pass this or direction.

params.name: ratio
params.description: The new pane's share of the space, in percent, from 1 to 99. Omit for an even split.

params.name: name
params.description: Name for the new window.

params.name: command
params.description: Argv to run in the new pane instead of a shell, as for new-window.

params.name: cwd
params.description: Directory to start in, as for new-window.

params.name: focus
params.description: Focus the new pane. Pass false to leave the focus where it is.

params.name: keep_open
params.description: Keep the pane after its process exits, as for new-window.

params.name: close_on_exit
params.description: Close the pane when its process exits, as for new-window.

params.name: env
params.description: Environment variables for the pane's process, as for new-window.

params.name: host
params.description: Run the pane's process on another machine, as for new-window.

params.name: shell_integration
params.description: Whether the pane's shell starts with OSC 133 prompt marks on, as for new-window.

params.name: grants
params.description: What the new pane may do through tuios: read, write, mail, fan, respond, files, task, admin, or none. Omit for the default of [agents.permissions], or, from a pane without admin, the calling pane's own grants. A pane may give only what it holds, and admin does not include respond. A window on another machine holds what that machine gives it.

returns.description: Id of the pane the split created.

returns.name: direction
returns.description: The axis that was cut.

returns.name: side
returns.description: The side the new pane took.

returns.name: name
returns.description: The new pane's name.

returns.name: workspace
returns.description: Workspace the new pane is on.

ssh-agent-path.description: Report the session's ssh agent link: the path that new panes get as SSH_AUTH_SOCK while [daemon] ssh_agent is follow, and the client socket it points at now.

params.name: session
params.description: Session whose link to report.

returns.name: session
returns.description: Session name.

returns.name: path
returns.description: The link. It exists only while an attached client has an agent socket.

returns.name: follow
returns.description: True when [daemon] ssh_agent is follow.

returns.name: target
returns.description: The client socket the link points at. Absent when there is no link.

start-agent.description: Start an agent in a new pane of a session and answer once it is ready for a prompt: its state reads idle or done, from a report, a hook, its screen or its title (unknown counts only for a harness that can never show idle). A pane on needs_input ends the wait at once with ready false and blocked_by, and is kept. With prompt, the first prompt is typed once it is ready, the way fan types it. A named session that does not exist is created. From another machine, address it with a host-qualified session and name the repository by repo_url.

params.name: session
params.description: Session to open the pane in. Created when it does not exist. Omit from a pane for the pane's own session. Outside every pane, omit for the most recently active session, or a new one named after the agent when there is none.

params.name: agent
params.description: The agent, as one string: a harness id or program name (claude, codex, gemini), or any program, with its arguments after it. Split the way a shell splits words and exec'd directly; nothing is expanded.

params.name: args
params.description: More arguments after the agent's own, as an argv. No shell parses them.

params.name: name
params.description: The window's name, which list-agents shows and -w takes, so the caller can address the agent as, say, reviewer.

params.name: cwd
params.description: The directory the agent starts in. Omit to use the calling pane's directory, or outside a pane the focused pane's. Pass cwd or a repository, not both.

params.name: repo
params.description: A directory inside a repository: the agent starts in its main checkout.

params.name: workspace
params.description: The workspace to open the pane on. Omit for the calling pane's workspace, else the one the session shows.

params.name: focus
params.description: Focus the new pane.

params.name: prompt
params.description: A first prompt, typed once the agent is ready and checked the way fan checks it.

params.name: ready_timeout
params.description: Milliseconds to wait for the agent to be ready.

params.name: no_wait
params.description: Answer once the agent's process has started and has not exited within a second, without waiting for it to be ready (outcome started). after_ready and prompt are then sent in the background once it is ready, and their status reads pending. An agent that stays unready shows in the Inbox.

params.name: env
params.description: Environment variables for the agent, name to value, on top of the daemon's; PATH in it is where the program is looked up first. A program not on it is looked up on the daemon's PATH, the one a new pane gets, and then runs with that PATH (path_from). The rules are fan's.

params.name: protocol
params.description: Run the agent headless over a structured protocol instead of in its own TUI: acp (the Agent Client Protocol, for an agent command such as "opencode acp") or codex (the Codex app-server; app-server is added to the codex command). The pane runs tuios agent-proto, which shows the conversation as a transcript and reports the agent's state itself; the pane is ready on that report alone. Its permission requests are answered in the pane or, for a request one line shows whole, from the Inbox without [agents.approvals]. Omit for the agent's own TUI.

params.name: task
params.description: A task card of the session, such as t3, for the new pane to work on: it is claimed for the pane as soon as the pane exists, before the wait. The caller needs what claim-task needs, and the card must be held by no pane, not blocked and not done, checked before anything is started. The session must exist already.

params.name: task_host
params.description: With task: the linked machine that owns the card. The new pane claims it there.

params.name: task_session
params.description: The card's session: there with task_host, else another session of this daemon. The pane's close lets the card go.

params.name: task_mail
params.description: With task: once the pane holds the card, mail it the card from tuios (title, prompt, and the commands that finish or release it), so nothing is typed into it.

params.name: human_nonce
params.description: With task: the attached client's nonce, so the claim is the person's (by human).

params.name: parent
params.description: The agent pane the new agent reports to, by window id or a unique start of it. Omit it from an agent pane: that pane is the parent. A pane may name itself or a pane it could type into, and the person may name any agent pane. A chain of agents stops at 8: a deeper start is refused.

params.name: model
params.description: The model, passed with the flag the harness's manifest names ([launch] model_flag). One word, not starting with -. Refused for a harness with no model flag.

params.name: effort
params.description: The effort, one of the harness's [launch] efforts, passed with its effort flag. Refused for a harness with no effort flag.

params.name: permission_mode
params.description: The permission mode, one of the harness's [launch] permissions, passed with its permission flag. From an agent pane it is held to the caller's own mode. Refused for a harness with no permission flag.

params.name: preset
params.description: An [agents.presets] entry of this daemon's config to start from. A param the call passes wins over the preset's; args, add_dirs and after_ready are the preset's then the call's; env is the preset's with the call's on top; grants the call passes replace the preset's. An unknown name is refused with the names there are.

params.name: add_dirs
params.description: More directories the agent may work in, each passed with the harness's [launch] add_dir_flag (Claude Code: --add-dir), before args. ~ is this machine's home folder. Refused for a harness with no such flag.

params.name: after_ready
params.description: Steps sent once the agent is ready, in order and before prompt: a step that is one key name (Enter, Escape, Tab, C-c) is that key, anything else is typed as text. A step is refused while the pane waits on a prompt of its own, which stops the rest.

params.name: grants
params.description: What the new pane may do through tuios: read, write, mail, fan, respond, files, task, admin, or none. Omit for the default of [agents.permissions], or, from a pane without admin, the calling pane's own grants. A pane may give only what it holds, and admin does not include respond. A window on another machine holds what that machine gives it.

params.name: repo_url
params.description: The repository by its origin URL, for a caller on another machine. This daemon finds its own checkout whose origin is the same repository. Pass repo or repo_url, not both.

params.name: repos_root
params.description: With repo_url, the directory on this machine to look under, and to clone into. Absolute, or starting with ~/. Omit to look under ~/src, ~/dev, ~/code, ~/projects, ~/repos, ~/git, ~/work, ~/go/src, the home directory itself and tuios's own clone directory.

params.name: clone
params.description: With repo_url, clone the repository when no checkout is found. Only https, ssh and git URLs are cloned.

returns.name: session
returns.description: The session the pane is in.

returns.name: session_id
returns.description: Id of the session.

returns.name: created_session
returns.description: True when the session was created by this call.

returns.name: pty_id
returns.description: Id of the new pane's PTY.

returns.name: workspace
returns.description: The workspace the pane is on.

returns.name: cwd
returns.description: The directory the agent started in, empty for the default.

returns.name: cloned
returns.description: True when the repository was cloned by this call. Absent otherwise.

returns.name: parent
returns.description: The parent agent pane, session and window, when the new agent has one. Absent otherwise.

returns.name: root
returns.description: The first agent of the parent chain, session and window, when the new agent has a parent. Absent otherwise.

returns.name: window_id
returns.description: The new pane.

returns.name: name
returns.description: Its name.

returns.name: agent
returns.description: The harness id, from the manifest or detection, empty when nothing recognises the program.

returns.name: command
returns.description: The command that was started. With protocol, the agent's command, which tuios agent-proto runs.

returns.name: protocol
returns.description: The protocol, when one was asked for. Absent otherwise.

returns.name: ready
returns.description: True when the agent showed it is at its prompt.

returns.name: ready_by
returns.description: The evidence: idle or done, or quiet for unknown on a harness that cannot show idle.

returns.name: state
returns.description: The pane's agent state when the wait ended.

returns.name: outcome
returns.description: How the wait ended. started is no_wait's answer: the process runs and readiness was not waited for. exited is no_wait's answer when the program exited within a second.

returns.name: path_from

returns.description: Why the after_ready steps were not all sent.

stream-pane.description: Stream one pane as bytes, for a client that is not tuios. The reply is one JSON line, and after it the connection carries binary frames both ways: a type byte, a 4-byte big-endian length, then the payload. From the daemon: S snapshot (u64 seq, u16 cols, u16 rows, then bytes that paint the pane on a fresh emulator of that size), O output (u64 seq after the frame's last byte, then the pane's bytes), R resize (u64 seq, u16 cols, u16 rows), E error (JSON code and message, for a refused frame or a lease that was not renewed; the stream goes on), X exit (the reason: exited N when the pane's program exited with status N, killed N when signal N ended it, closed when its window closed first, or refused: … when the caller may no longer read it; the connection then closes). From the client: I input (at most 64 KiB of bytes typed into the pane, checked as send-text is), L lease (u16 cols, u16 rows, 0 0 to release; send it again every 10 seconds, or the lease ends after 30). Skip a frame type you do not know: read its length and drop that many bytes. At most 4 I frames wait for a pane that does not read, and the next gets E busy. The stream never changes the pane's size or the session's. A lease holds the pane at most at its size while the stream is open, and the pane goes back to the size its clients asked for when the lease ends.

params.name: session
params.description: Session name. Omit from a pane for the pane's own session, and from outside every pane for the most recently active one.

params.name: window
params.description: The pane to stream: a window id or name.

params.name: from_seq
params.description: The seq the client reached on an earlier stream of this pane. With boot_id, the stream resumes there when the daemon still holds the bytes after it.

params.name: boot_id
params.description: The boot_id of the stream from_seq came from. A different one means the daemon restarted, and the stream starts with a snapshot.

params.name: lease_cols
params.description: Hold the pane at most this many columns wide while the stream is open. Needs lease_rows. It needs what resize needs.

params.name: lease_rows
params.description: Hold the pane at most this many rows high while the stream is open. Needs lease_cols.

params.name: session_id
params.description: The session by its id, which a rename does not change. It wins over session. The reply carries it.

params.name: fit
params.description: Make the lease a viewer's: while no TUI client shows the session, the pane takes the size of the largest fit lease held, and goes back to its own size when the last one ends. While a client shows the session, a fit lease only holds the pane smaller.

params.name: viewer
params.description: The terminal the stream shows the pane in: bg, fg (#rrggbb), palette (sixteen comma-separated #rrggbb), kitty and sixel (bool). While no TUI client shows the session, the daemon answers the pane's OSC 10, 11 and 4, DA1 and kitty graphics queries from the newest viewer's report.

returns.name: mode
returns.description: resume: the first frames are output from from_seq. snapshot: the first frame is S.

returns.name: seq
returns.description: The stream position the first frame starts at.

returns.name: cols
returns.description: The pane's width at seq.

returns.name: rows
returns.description: The pane's height at seq.

returns.name: boot_id
returns.description: This daemon start. Send it back with from_seq to resume.

returns.name: session
returns.description: The pane's session.

returns.name: session_id
returns.description: The pane's session id, which a rename does not change.

returns.name: window
returns.description: The pane's window id.

returns.name: title
returns.description: The pane's title.

subscribe.description: Open a long-lived event stream on this connection. Without after_seq, events start at the moment of subscription. With after_seq, the stream first replays the retained events after that seq, so a reconnecting subscriber gets what it missed, and sends a gap marker with a reason when it cannot.

params.name: session
params.description: Only deliver events from this session. Omit for events from every session. Unlike most verbs, an omitted session does not mean the most recently active one.

params.name: window
params.description: Only deliver events about this window id. Omit for every window.

params.name: types
params.description: Only deliver these event types. Omit for all of them.

params.name: queue
params.description: Buffered events before the stream marks a gap. A size above 4096 is lowered to 4096.

params.name: after_seq
params.description: Resume: replay the retained events with a seq above this one before streaming live. Pass the seq of the last event received. 0 replays everything the daemon still holds. Output events are not retained.

params.name: boot_id
params.description: The boot_id the after_seq came with. If the daemon has restarted since, the stream starts with a gap marker with reason boot_changed instead of a replay. Needs after_seq.

params.name: hosts
params.description: Also deliver the agent-state, session-created and session-closed events this daemon relays from its linked hosts, each carrying host, and let session and window match events of other machines. Without it an event about another machine reaches only a subscriber that names no session or window, and only an attention or host-changed event.

returns.name: seq
returns.description: The last seq assigned when the stream went live. Every live event has a higher seq, and every replayed event has this seq or lower.

returns.name: boot_id
returns.description: Random id of this daemon start. Keep it with the seq, and pass both back to resume.

returns.name: replayed
returns.description: With after_seq only: how many events are replayed before the live stream.

swap-window.description: Swap two tiled panes of one workspace. Works with no client attached. The focus stays where it is.

params.name: session
params.description: Session name. Omit from a pane for the pane's own session, and from outside every pane for the most recently active one.

params.name: window
params.description: One pane. Omit for the caller's own pane, or outside a pane the focused one.

params.name: with
params.description: The other pane.

returns.name: window_id
returns.description: Id of the first pane.

returns.name: with
returns.description: Id of the other pane.

switch-session.description: Switch an attached client to another session in place, as go-to does. The client is the one named by client, else the one showing session, else the one showing the caller's own session from a pane, else the only one attached.

params.name: name
params.description: Session to switch to.

params.name: host
params.description: Machine from the client's [hosts] table that holds the session. Omit, or local, for this daemon.

params.name: create
params.description: Create the session when it does not exist.

params.name: cwd
params.description: With create, the directory the new session's windows start in.

params.name: session
params.description: Session the client to switch shows.

params.name: client
params.description: Id of the client to switch, from list-clients.

returns.name: session
returns.description: Session the client now shows.

returns.name: host
returns.description: Machine the session is on. Absent for this daemon.

returns.name: client_id
returns.description: Id of the client that switched.

returns.name: created
returns.description: True when create made the session on this daemon.

returns.name: already
returns.description: True when the client already showed the session. Nothing changed.

tml-close.description: Close a TML surface and its window. A tml-open that waits on it answers with the value.

params.name: surface
params.description: The surface id tml-open answered with.

params.name: value
params.description: A JSON value for the waiting caller. Omit for null.

returns.name: surface
returns.description: The surface that closed.

tml-get.description: Read a TML surface: its tree as TML JSON, its state and its version.

params.name: surface
params.description: The surface id.

returns.name: doc
returns.description: The tree as TML JSON, with the state it was opened with.

returns.name: state
returns.description: The state now.

returns.name: version
returns.description: The version: it counts every change of the tree or the state.

returns.name: window_id
returns.description: The window the surface is drawn in.

returns.name: title
returns.description: The surface's title.

returns.name: owner
returns.description: Who opened it: a pane, or tuios tml show.

tml-input.description: Report what the person did on a TML surface: the state its local actions changed, and a close. The attached client sends it, with its attach nonce.

params.name: surface
params.description: The surface id.

params.name: human_nonce
params.description: The attach nonce of the person's client.

params.name: ops
params.description: A JSON Patch (RFC 6902) on the surface's state.

params.name: close
params.description: Close the surface.

params.name: value
params.description: With close: the value. Omit when the person dismissed the surface.

params.name: events
params.description: The emit actions the person ran, each {name, value}. Each becomes a tml-event for the owner.

params.name: actions
params.description: The pane() actions the person ran, each {verb, params}: focus, new-window or send-text. Each runs with the grants of the pane that opened the surface, never the person's.

params.name: view
params.description: The client's view state, as loom keeps it: open tabs, cursor rows, scroll places, sorts, filters and folds, without typed text. capture-pane draws the surface with the last view reported.

returns.name: version
returns.description: The surface's version after the change.

returns.name: actions
returns.description: Each pane() action's result: verb, ok, and error and code when it was refused.

tml-list.description: List the open TML surfaces of a session.

params.name: session
params.description: Session name. Omit from a pane for the pane's own session, and from outside every pane for the most recently active one.

returns.name: surfaces
returns.description: Each surface: surface, window_id, title, owner and version.

tml-open.description: Show a TML document as a popup or a pane. Every attached client draws it, and the daemon keeps it while nobody is attached.

params.name: session
params.description: Session name. Omit from a pane for the pane's own session, and from outside every pane for the most recently active one.

params.name: doc
params.description: The document: TML text or TML JSON as a string, or a TML JSON object. It is checked as tml-validate checks it, and a document with errors is refused with invalid_tml and the problem list.

params.name: target
params.description: Where to show it: popup, a floating box over the panes that needs an attached client, or pane, a tiled pane.

params.name: name
params.description: Name for the window. Omit to use the document's title.

params.name: width
params.description: Popup width, in cells ("60") or as a share of the pane region ("60%"). Popup only.

params.name: height
params.description: Popup height, in cells ("20") or as a share of the pane region ("50%"). Popup only.

params.name: workspace
params.description: Workspace to open it on. Omit for the current one.

params.name: wait
params.description: Keep the call open until the surface closes, and return the close value in a tml_result.

params.name: timeout
params.description: With wait: milliseconds to wait before failing with the timeout code. The surface stays open. 0 waits as long as it is open.

params.name: events
params.description: Keep the connection and stream the surface's tml-event events on it after the answer, as subscribe does: each emit, and the close as the last one. Not with wait.

returns.name: surface
returns.description: Id of the surface. Use it to patch, replace, read or close the surface.

returns.name: seq
returns.description: With events: the last event number when the stream went live, as subscribe answers.

returns.name: boot_id
returns.description: With events: the daemon start that numbers the events.

returns.name: window_id
returns.description: Id of the window the surface is drawn in.

returns.name: target
returns.description: popup or pane.

returns.name: workspace
returns.description: Workspace the surface was opened on.

returns.name: value
returns.description: With wait: the value the surface closed with. null when the person dismissed it.

returns.name: reason
returns.description: With wait: closed when the person ran a close action, so the value is the person's answer; program when a tml-close gave the value; dismissed when the window closed without one.

tml-patch.description: Change a TML surface's state with a JSON Patch (RFC 6902). Only the parts of the surface that read the changed paths are drawn again.

params.name: surface
params.description: The surface id tml-open answered with.

params.name: ops
params.description: The JSON Patch: add, remove, replace, move, copy and test operations on the state. A test that does not match refuses the whole patch, so read the state again with tml-get.

returns.name: version
returns.description: The surface's version after the patch.

returns.name: changed
returns.description: The JSON Pointers the patch changed.

tml-place.description: Move a TML surface between a popup and a tiled pane, as the person chose. The surface keeps its state, so a form keeps what the person typed. Needs the attach nonce of a client.

params.name: surface
params.description: The surface id.

params.name: target
params.description: popup or pane.

params.name: human_nonce
params.description: The attach nonce of the client the person uses.

returns.name: window_id
returns.description: The surface's window.

returns.name: target
returns.description: Where the surface is now.

tml-replace.description: Swap a TML surface's tree. Each client keeps its view state (the open tab, the cursor row) for the nodes whose ids stay.

params.name: surface
params.description: The surface id.

params.name: doc
params.description: The new document, as tml-open takes it.

params.name: keep_state
params.description: Keep the state the surface has now instead of the new document's state.

returns.name: version
returns.description: The surface's version after the swap.

tml-validate.description: Check a TML document as tml-open would. Needs no session.

params.name: doc
params.description: The document: TML text or TML JSON as a string, or a TML JSON object.

returns.name: warnings
returns.description: The warnings, each with at, code and message. A document with errors fails with invalid_tml instead.

wait-dir.description: Wait until the names in a directory on this machine change: a file added, removed or renamed. The daemon that owns a window on another machine asks it, so the rail's file section can follow that machine's disk. It answers changed false when the timeout ends first.

params.name: dir
params.description: The directory to watch.

params.name: timeout
params.description: Milliseconds to wait. Omit for 30 seconds.

params.name: after
params.description: The names value of the last answer. When the names differ from it, the wait answers at once with changed true.

returns.name: dir
returns.description: The directory watched.

returns.name: changed
returns.description: The names changed before the timeout ended.

returns.name: names
returns.description: A short sum of the names in the directory, empty when they cannot be read or there are more than 100000.

wait-for.description: Block until a condition matches, or fail with the timeout code.

params.name: condition
params.description: Condition to wait for.

params.name: session
params.description: Session name. session-exists requires it: it is the session to wait for. For the other conditions, omit it from a pane for the pane's own session, and from outside every pane for the most recently active one.

params.name: window
params.description: Window id or name. Omit to target the focused window.

params.name: any_session
params.description: For agent-state only: watch every session on the daemon, including ones created during the wait. Takes no session or window. The result names the session that matched.

params.name: pattern
params.description: Regular expression, required by window-output.

params.name: source
params.description: Which buffer window-output matches against. The default includes scrollback, so output that has already scrolled past still matches.

params.name: new
params.description: For window-output: match only the output the pane writes after the wait starts. Text already on the screen or in the scrollback does not match. A program that redraws its screen writes its text again, and that text matches. Takes no source.

params.name: idle
params.description: Milliseconds of silence that count as idle, for window-idle.

params.name: until
params.description: Agent state(s) to wait for, comma-separated, required by agent-state. With no window, any window in the session reaching one of them matches.

params.name: thread
params.description: Narrow agent-message to one thread. Pass any message id in the thread. A thread the ring holds nothing from never matches.

params.name: command_seq
params.description: For command-finished with a window: match once the pane has finished more commands than this, which is already true when the command finished before the wait. Read it from list-windows or a run timeout. Without it, the next command to finish after the wait starts matches.

params.name: timeout
params.description: Milliseconds to wait before failing with the timeout code, at most 86400000 (24 hours). The wait also ends when the caller closes the connection.

params.name: select
params.description: A selector: space-separated key:value terms, all of which must match, each with comma-separated alternatives. Keys: harness (id or program name), state, needs:you, session (glob), group (fan-out group, glob), host (local or a host name, glob), name (window name, glob), cwd (the directory or under it; ~ is home), task (a task card the pane holds, by id, glob), stage (the stage of a card the pane holds), parent and root (the parent agent pane, or the first of its chain, by window id or a start of it). For agent-state only: watch the agent panes it matches, in every session, including panes that open during the wait. Takes no session, window or any_session. Put the state to wait for in until, not in the selector.

params.name: under
params.description: With select: watch only the panes that this window started, and the panes they started, by window id. A pane with the fan grant and without admin always waits under its own window.

params.name: every
params.description: With select: match only when at least one pane matches and every matched pane is in one of the until states, and answer with all of them in panes. Without it, the first matched pane to reach one matches.

params.name: name
params.description: The hold to wait for, required by hold-released. It matches at once when no one holds it, and otherwise when its holder releases it, its ttl ends or its holder pane closes.

returns.name: condition
returns.description: The condition that matched.

returns.name: window
returns.description: The window that matched, for a condition about a window.

returns.name: exit_code
returns.description: For window-exit and command-finished: the exit status, -1 when a signal ended the process. Omitted when it is not known, such as for a window on another machine.

returns.name: signal
returns.description: For window-exit: the signal that ended the process. Omitted when it exited on its own.

returns.name: new
returns.description: For window-output: true when the wait matched only output written after it started.

zoom-window.description: Zoom a pane to fill its workspace, or end the zoom. Works with no client attached. Zooming a pane on the workspace the session shows focuses it.

params.name: session
params.description: Session name. Omit from a pane for the pane's own session, and from outside every pane for the most recently active one.

params.name: window
params.description: Window to zoom. Omit for the caller's own pane, or outside a pane the focused one.

params.name: zoom
params.description: True to zoom, false to end the zoom on the window's workspace. Omit to toggle.

returns.name: window_id
returns.description: Id of the window.

returns.name: zoomed
returns.description: Whether the window is zoomed now.

returns.name: changed
returns.description: False when the zoom was already as asked.
